# Search button: `jl-search-button`

What opens the command palette: a search field to press, with its keys.

- Class `JlSearchButton`, a molecule: `import { JlSearchButton } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/search-button

The search button sits at the top of an app's side nav and opens its command palette. It looks like a
search field, so people know they can type, and shows the palette's keys (Ctrl K, ⌘K on a Mac) so they learn them.
Touch screens have no keys: there it shows none.

compact keeps the icon alone: in a folded side nav, or in a phone's top bar. The keys are the palette's own: the
button only shows them, and fires press when clicked. See the Search and shortcuts pattern.

## Use

```ts
import { JlSearchButton } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlSearchButton hotkey="mod+k" label="Search" />
```

```html
<jl-search-button hotkey="mod+k" label="Search"></jl-search-button>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. Its text, and its name for screen readers. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.
- `hotkey` (attribute `hotkey`): `string`, default `'mod+k'`. The keys it shows, as jl-kbd writes them; none for no keys.
- `compact` (attribute `compact`): `boolean`, default `false`. The icon alone, the label as its tooltip.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `press` (`onPress` in JSX), detail `undefined`: The button was pressed: open the palette.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The button.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### In a side nav

At the top of a side nav: it fills the width.

```html
<div style="width: 240px; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--jl-line); border-radius: var(--jl-radius-lg)">
  <jl-search-button></jl-search-button>
</div>
```

### Opening the palette

Pressed, it opens a command palette (its own keys turned off here: the site has Ctrl K).

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-search-button class="demo-open" style="width: 220px"></jl-search-button>
  <jl-search-button class="demo-open" compact></jl-search-button>
</div>
<jl-command-palette class="demo-palette" hotkey="none" commands='[{"group":"Go to","icon":"list","id":"orders","label":"Orders"},{"group":"Go to","icon":"package","id":"stock","label":"Stock"},{"group":"Actions","icon":"plus","id":"new","label":"New order…"}]'></jl-command-palette>
```

```js
const palette = root.querySelector('.demo-palette');
for (const button of root.querySelectorAll('.demo-open')) {
  button.events.register('press', () => palette.show());
}
```
